title: [Ubuntu, macOS, Windows] Go 1.24 will be removed from the tool-cache and the default Go version will be updated to 1.26 starting November 18, 2026
body:
### Breaking changes

Starting **November 18, 2026**, the following changes will be rolled out to the runner images:

- Go `1.27.*` will be added to the tool-cache.
- Go `1.24.*` will be removed from the tool-cache.
- The default Go version (the `go` binary on `PATH`) will be updated from `1.24.*` to `1.26.*` on Ubuntu 22.04, Ubuntu 24.04 and all Windows images. Ubuntu 26.04 already uses `1.26.*` as the default, so its default doesn't change.

After this change, the following Go versions will be available in the tool-cache on all images: `1.25.*`, `1.26.*`, `1.27.*`.

macOS images don't have a default Go version on `PATH`, so only the tool-cache versions change there.

| Image | Go versions before | Go versions after | Default before | Default after |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Ubuntu 22.04, Ubuntu 22.04 Arm64 | `1.24.*`, `1.25.*`, `1.26.*` | `1.25.*`, `1.26.*`, `1.27.*` | `1.24.*` | `1.26.*` |
| Ubuntu 24.04, Ubuntu 24.04 Arm64 | `1.24.*`, `1.25.*`, `1.26.*` | `1.25.*`, `1.26.*`, `1.27.*` | `1.24.*` | `1.26.*` |
| Ubuntu 26.04, Ubuntu 26.04 Arm64 | `1.24.*`, `1.25.*`, `1.26.*` | `1.25.*`, `1.26.*`, `1.27.*` | `1.26.*` | `1.26.*` (no change) |
| macOS 15, macOS 15 Arm64 | `1.24.*`, `1.25.*`, `1.26.*` | `1.25.*`, `1.26.*`, `1.27.*` | not set | not set |
| macOS 26, macOS 26 Arm64 | `1.24.*`, `1.25.*`, `1.26.*` | `1.25.*`, `1.26.*`, `1.27.*` | not set | not set |
| Xcode 27 | `1.24.*`, `1.25.*`, `1.26.*` | `1.25.*`, `1.26.*`, `1.27.*` | not set | not set |
| Windows Server 2022 | `1.24.*`, `1.25.*`, `1.26.*` | `1.25.*`, `1.26.*`, `1.27.*` | `1.24.*` | `1.26.*` |
| Windows Server 2025 | `1.24.*`, `1.25.*`, `1.26.*` | `1.25.*`, `1.26.*`, `1.27.*` | `1.24.*` | `1.26.*` |
| Windows Server 2025 with Visual Studio 2026 | `1.24.*`, `1.25.*`, `1.26.*` | `1.25.*`, `1.26.*`, `1.27.*` | `1.24.*` | `1.26.*` |
| Windows Desktop 11 | `1.24.*`, `1.25.*`, `1.26.*` | `1.25.*`, `1.26.*`, `1.27.*` | `1.24.*` | `1.26.*` |
| Windows Desktop 11 with Visual Studio 2026 | `1.24.*`, `1.25.*`, `1.26.*` | `1.25.*`, `1.26.*`, `1.27.*` | `1.24.*` | `1.26.*` |

### Target date

The rollout will start no earlier than **November 18, 2026**. The exact start may shift by a few days if issues come up during image validation. Once started, deployment usually takes 2-3 days to reach all regions.

### The motivation for the changes

The [software and image support policy](https://github.com/actions/runner-images#software-and-image-support) keeps the 3 latest Go minor versions on the images. Go 1.27 was released in August 2026, and Go 1.24 is no longer supported by the Go team.

The new default, Go 1.26, is the same as the default on Ubuntu 26.04, so all Ubuntu and Windows images will use the same default Go version.

### Possible impact

- Workflows that rely on the preinstalled `go` binary on Ubuntu 22.04, Ubuntu 24.04 or Windows will use Go 1.26 instead of Go 1.24.
- Go 1.25 and Go 1.26 include changes that can affect builds moving from Go 1.24. See the [Go 1.25](https://go.dev/doc/go1.25) and [Go 1.26](https://go.dev/doc/go1.26) release notes.
- Workflows that request Go 1.24 through `actions/setup-go` or the Azure DevOps Go Tool task will download it during the run instead of using the tool-cache. This can make the setup step slower and depend on network availability.
- Workflows that read the `GOROOT_1_24_X64`, `GOROOT_1_24_ARM64` or `GOROOT_1_24_AARCH64` environment variables will no longer find them.

Workflows that already pin Go 1.25, 1.26 or 1.27 aren't affected.

### Platforms affected

- [x] Azure DevOps
- [x] GitHub Actions

### Runner images affected

- [x] Ubuntu 22.04
- [x] Ubuntu 22.04 Arm64
- [x] Ubuntu 24.04
- [x] Ubuntu 24.04 Arm64
- [x] Ubuntu 26.04
- [x] Ubuntu 26.04 Arm64
- [ ] Ubuntu Slim
- [ ] macOS 14
- [ ] macOS 14 Arm64
- [x] macOS 15
- [x] macOS 15 Arm64
- [x] macOS 26
- [x] macOS 26 Arm64
- [x] Windows Server 2022
- [x] Windows Server 2025
- [x] Windows Server 2025 with Visual Studio 2026
- [x] Windows Desktop 11
- [x] Windows Desktop 11 with Visual Studio 2026

### Mitigation ways

We recommend moving to a supported Go version. If you need to keep a specific version, pin it explicitly instead of relying on the image default.

GitHub Actions, using [`actions/setup-go`](https://github.com/actions/setup-go):

```yaml
- uses: actions/setup-go@v7
  with:
    go-version: '1.24'
```

To always use the version from your module, use `go-version-file: 'go.mod'` instead of `go-version`.

Azure DevOps, using the [Go Tool task](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/devops/pipelines/tasks/reference/go-tool-v0?view=azure-pipelines):

```yaml
- task: GoTool@0
  inputs:
    version: '1.24.13'
```

title: [macOS] Azure DevOps macOS 14 Intel runners extended through November 23, 2026
body:
### Breaking changes

The macOS 14 retirement remains in effect for GitHub Actions and Azure DevOps macOS 14 arm64 images on November 2, 2026. **Azure DevOps macOS 14 Intel images only are extended through November 23, 2026.** This extension does not apply to GitHub Actions or arm64 images.

To raise awareness of the upcoming Azure DevOps Intel retirement, jobs using these images will temporarily fail during the brownout periods below. All dates and times are in UTC:

- November 5, 14:00 - November 6, 00:00
- November 12, 14:00 - November 13, 00:00
- November 15, 14:00 - November 16, 00:00
- November 19, 14:00 - November 20, 00:00

### Target date

GitHub Actions macOS 14 (Intel and arm64): November 2, 2026
Azure DevOps macOS 14 arm64: November 2, 2026
Azure DevOps macOS 14 Intel: November 23, 2026

### The motivation for the changes

Azure DevOps Intel customers need additional time to migrate from macOS 14. This temporary extension applies only to Azure DevOps Intel SKUs; GitHub Actions continues with the planned macOS 14 retirement.

### Possible impact

Azure DevOps jobs using macOS 14 Intel images will fail during the listed brownouts and after retirement on November 23, 2026. GitHub Actions macOS 14 jobs and Azure DevOps macOS 14 arm64 jobs are not extended and retire on November 2, 2026.

Please update the Azure DevOps/MMS retirement error message to tell customers that macOS 14 Intel images will retire on November 23, 2026, so customers are not confused by the extension. The GitHub Actions retirement date remains November 2, 2026.

### Platforms affected

- [x] Azure DevOps
- [x] GitHub Actions

### Runner images affected

- [x] macOS 14
- [ ] macOS 14 Arm64

### Mitigation ways

- GitHub Actions workflows using macOS 14 labels and Azure DevOps workflows using macOS 14 arm64 images should migrate to supported images; these are not extended beyond November 2, 2026.
- Azure DevOps workflows using macOS 14 Intel labels should migrate before November 23, 2026.

title: [macOS] The default OpenSSL version will be updated from 3 to 4 on macOS 26 and Xcode 27
body:
### Breaking changes

The default `openssl` command will change from **OpenSSL 3.x** to **OpenSSL 4.x** on macOS 26 Intel/Arm64 and Xcode 27 Arm64 runner images.

We will remove the explicit selection of OpenSSL 3 as the default CLI. OpenSSL 4 is already installed on these images; this change makes it the version used when workflows invoke `openssl` without an explicit versioned path.

OpenSSL 3 will remain installed and available through its versioned Homebrew prefix. This announcement does not remove OpenSSL 3 or change the OpenSSL defaults on macOS 14/15, Ubuntu, or Windows images.

### Target date

The rollout is planned to begin on **November 2, 2026** and complete by **November 8, 2026**, subject to compatibility validation. Updated images will be deployed gradually during this period.

### The motivation for the changes

Homebrew's unversioned `openssl` formula now resolves to OpenSSL 4. Our images currently select OpenSSL 3 explicitly to preserve the existing default while users prepare for the major-version transition.

This planned change aligns the default CLI with Homebrew's current default and gives users advance notice to validate their workflows. The default-version migration is separate from the earlier compatibility fix that retained OpenSSL 3.

### Possible impact

- Workflows that invoke `openssl` through `PATH` will use OpenSSL 4 instead of OpenSSL 3.
- Scripts that check for major version 3 or depend on version-specific command options, output, or defaults may need updates. Test certificate, key, signing, and TLS-related commands before the rollout.

### Platforms affected

- [x] Azure DevOps
- [x] GitHub Actions

### Runner images affected

- [ ] Ubuntu 22.04
- [ ] Ubuntu 22.04 Arm64
- [ ] Ubuntu 24.04
- [ ] Ubuntu 24.04 Arm64
- [ ] Ubuntu 26.04
- [ ] Ubuntu 26.04 Arm64
- [ ] Ubuntu Slim
- [ ] macOS 14
- [ ] macOS 14 Arm64
- [ ] macOS 15
- [ ] macOS 15 Arm64
- [x] macOS 26
- [x] macOS 26 Arm64
- [x] Xcode 27 Arm64
- [ ] Windows Server 2022
- [ ] Windows Server 2025
- [ ] Windows Server 2025 with Visual Studio 2026
- [ ] Windows Desktop 11
- [ ] Windows Desktop 11 with Visual Studio 2026

### Mitigation ways

If your workflow requires a specific OpenSSL version, select it explicitly in your workflow or build configuration rather than relying on the image's default. OpenSSL 3 will remain available for workflows that need it.

Workflows that use the default OpenSSL command without explicitly selecting a version will automatically switch to OpenSSL 4 as the updated runner images are rolled out.

title: [Windows 11 Arm] Android CMake will be updated to 3.30.5, 3.31.5 and 4.1.2
body:
### Breaking changes

On the Windows 11 Arm images, the Android SDK CMake versions will be updated to match Windows Server 2025. `3.18.1` and `3.22.1` will be removed, and `3.30.5`, `3.31.5` and `4.1.2` will be installed under `%ANDROID_HOME%\cmake\<version>`.

### Target date

2026-10-15

### The motivation for the changes

* The Windows 11 Arm images still ship old CMake versions (`3.18.1` / `3.22.1`), while Windows Server 2025 already ships `3.30.5` / `3.31.5` / `4.1.2`
* Brings the Arm images in line with the x64 images
* Requested in #14721

### Possible impact

* Workflows that pin `cmake;3.18.1` or `cmake;3.22.1` (for example `externalNativeBuild { cmake { version "3.22.1" } }`) will no longer find that version
* Projects with `cmake_minimum_required` below `3.5` will fail under CMake `4.1.2` with `Compatibility with CMake < 3.5 has been removed from CMake.`

### Platforms affected

- [ ] Azure DevOps
- [x] GitHub Actions

### Runner images affected

- [ ] Ubuntu 22.04
- [ ] Ubuntu 22.04 Arm64
- [ ] Ubuntu 24.04
- [ ] Ubuntu 24.04 Arm64
- [ ] Ubuntu 26.04
- [ ] Ubuntu 26.04 Arm64
- [ ] Ubuntu Slim
- [ ] macOS 14
- [ ] macOS 14 Arm64
- [ ] macOS 15
- [ ] macOS 15 Arm64
- [ ] macOS 26
- [ ] macOS 26 Arm64
- [ ] Windows Server 2022
- [ ] Windows Server 2025
- [ ] Windows Server 2025 with Visual Studio 2026
- [x] Windows Desktop 11
- [x] Windows Desktop 11 with Visual Studio 2026

### Mitigation ways

* Update any pinned CMake version to `3.30.5` or `3.31.5`
* For the CMake 4.x error, raise `cmake_minimum_required` to `3.5` or higher (`3.10`+ avoids deprecation warnings), or pin `3.30.5` / `3.31.5`

title: [Windows] MySQL will be updated from 8.0 to 8.4
body:
### Breaking changes

MySQL is being updated from 8.0 to the 8.4 LTS line on all Windows images. `mysql -V` will report 8.4.x instead of 8.0.x.

### Target date

2026-10-13

### The motivation for the changes

* MySQL 8.0 reaches end of life on 2026-04-30; 8.4 is the current LTS (supported until 2032)
* Requested in #14736

### Possible impact

MySQL 8.4 removes several long-deprecated server options and system variables, and the `mysql_native_password` auth plugin is no longer enabled by default. Workflows that start the bundled MySQL server and rely on those may need config changes; most client-only usage is unaffected.

### Platforms affected

- [x] Azure DevOps
- [x] GitHub Actions

### Runner images affected

- [ ] Ubuntu 22.04
- [ ] Ubuntu 22.04 Arm64
- [ ] Ubuntu 24.04
- [ ] Ubuntu 24.04 Arm64
- [ ] Ubuntu 26.04
- [ ] Ubuntu 26.04 Arm64
- [ ] Ubuntu Slim
- [ ] macOS 14
- [ ] macOS 14 Arm64
- [ ] macOS 15
- [ ] macOS 15 Arm64
- [ ] macOS 26
- [ ] macOS 26 Arm64
- [x] Windows Server 2022
- [x] Windows Server 2025
- [x] Windows Server 2025 with Visual Studio 2026
- [x] Windows Desktop 11
- [x] Windows Desktop 11 with Visual Studio 2026

### Mitigation ways

* For clients needing the old auth plugin, start the server with `--mysql-native-password=ON` or switch users to `caching_sha2_password`
* Pin your own MySQL 8.0 install in the workflow if you need the old version
